skill.name: parallel-task
skill.description: Coordinate explicit slash-command plan execution with dependency-aware parallel subagent waves.
skill.summary: Runs markdown implementation plans through dependency-aware parallel agent waves.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced examples in SKILL.md. No evidence found of executable Ruby, shell commands, prompt injection, credential access, network calls, or exfiltration intent.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Find task subsections (e.g., `### T1:` or `### Task 1.1:`)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 23 uses Markdown inline code to show example task headings. It is documentation text, not Ruby backtick execution or a shell command.

Line 86 closes the same Markdown fenced prompt template. A closing fence cannot execute commands and provides no command injection path.
Line 113 opens a Markdown fenced example usage block. The examples show slash-command text, not shell backticks or executable code.

content.value_statement: Large implementation plans are hard to coordinate across multiple agents. This skill turns a markdown plan into dependency-aware waves for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Parses markdown plan files for task IDs, names, dependencies, and task content.
Filters requested task subsets while including required dependency tasks.
Launches all currently unblocked tasks in parallel agent waves.
Provides subagents with plan context, acceptance criteria, validation steps, and constraints.
Checks task completion, plan log updates, and validation results after each wave.
Defines an execution summary format for completed, blocked, and failed tasks.
limitations: Requires a well-structured markdown plan with task headings and depends_on fields.
Depends on the host agent environment for subagent orchestration support.
Does not create project-specific tests or acceptance criteria on its own.
Instructs agents to commit completed work, but explicitly tells them not to push.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Work
use_cases.description: Break a feature plan into dependency-aware waves and assign ready tasks to separate agents.

use_cases.title: Finish Backlog Plans
use_cases.description: Run selected tasks from a larger plan while preserving required prerequisite work.

use_cases.title: Validate Parallel Changes
use_cases.description: Review agent outputs, confirm plan logs, and retry incomplete tasks before starting the next wave.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a complete implementation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task ./plans/release-plan.md
Read the full plan, execute all unblocked tasks in dependency order, and update the plan after each task.

prompt_templates.title: Run Selected Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for a limited task subset.
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task ./plans/auth-plan.md T1 T2 T4
Run only these tasks and include any dependencies required to complete them safely.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Feature Build
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for parallel implementation and validation.
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task ./plans/profile-plan.md
Use parallel waves where dependencies allow. Validate each task against its acceptance criteria before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a Partial Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for interrupted or failed plan execution.
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task ./plans/migration-plan.md
Review task logs, identify completed work, retry failed tasks, and continue until all remaining tasks are validated.

output_examples.input: A feature plan with setup tasks, API tasks, UI tasks, and validation tasks.
output_examples.output: Wave 1 completes setup. Wave 2 assigns API and UI work. The final summary lists changed files and validation results.

output_examples.input: A request to run selected authentication tasks from a larger plan.
output_examples.output: The skill includes required dependencies, skips unrelated tasks, records task logs, and reports any blockers before continuing.

output_examples.input: A migration plan where one task fails validation.
output_examples.output: The skill escalates the failed task for retry, keeps dependent tasks blocked, and resumes the next wave after validation passes.

best_practices: Write clear task headings, stable task IDs, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation steps before running the skill.
Keep each task small enough for one agent to complete, validate, and document in the plan.
Review commits and plan logs between waves when tasks touch shared files or migrations.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague task descriptions that omit files, acceptance criteria, or validation expectations.
Do not run unrelated tasks in the same wave when they edit the same high-risk files.
Do not treat a task as complete until the plan log and validation evidence are updated.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a markdown development plan contains tasks that can be assigned in dependency-aware waves.

faq.question: Does it require a specific plan format?
faq.answer: Yes. The plan should use task headings and explicit depends_on lists so dependencies can be parsed.

faq.question: Can I run only part of a plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide task IDs, and the skill includes the required dependencies for those selected tasks.

faq.question: Does it push changes to GitHub?
faq.answer: No. The skill tells agents to commit their own work and never push changes.

faq.question: How does it handle failed tasks?
faq.answer: It asks for retry or escalation, keeps dependent tasks blocked, and continues only after validation succeeds.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code environments with compatible agent orchestration.
